# Setup
---

paragraphs.title: Generate the data
paragraphs.text:
%sh

rm -rf  /var/lib/zeppelin/tmp/tpcds
mkdir -p  /var/lib/zeppelin/tmp/tpcds
cd /home/training/training_materials/perf/tpcds-kit/tools
./dsdgen -SCALE 1 -DIR /var/lib/zeppelin/tmp/tpcds

paragraphs.title: Put the data in HDFS
paragraphs.text:
%sh

hdfs dfs -mkdir -p /spark-perf/tpcds/customer
hdfs dfs -put -f  /var/lib/zeppelin/tmp/tpcds/customer.dat /spark-perf/tpcds/customer

paragraphs.title: Note
paragraphs.text:
%md
The database and tables we created via Spark are considered external by default.
You can see the  'TRANSLATED_TO_EXTERNAL' property is set to 'TRUE',
Thus we were able to freely write to and read from those tables.
To create a real managed table by Hive, we will need an additional connector.

%md
## Working with Databases and Tables managed by Hive

paragraphs.title: Create the Hive managed database
paragraphs.text:
%jdbc(hive)

DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS hivedb CASCADE;

CREATE DATABASE hivedb;
USE hivedb;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS  customer_hive_managed (
                                        c_customer_sk bigint,
                                        c_customer_id string,
                                        c_current_cdemo_sk bigint,
                                        c_current_hdemo_sk bigint,
                                        c_current_addr_sk bigint,
                                        c_first_shipto_date_sk bigint,
                                        c_first_sales_date_sk bigint,
                                        c_salutation string,
                                        c_first_name string,
                                        c_last_name string,
                                        c_preferred_cust_flag string,
                                        c_birth_day int,
                                        c_birth_month int,
                                        c_birth_year int,
                                        c_birth_country string,
                                        c_login string,
                                        c_email_address string,
                                        c_last_review_date string);

paragraphs.title: Confirm successful creation of the database and table
paragraphs.text:
%spark

spark.sql("show databases").show()
spark.sql("use hivedb")
spark.sql("show tables").show()

paragraphs.title: Inspect customer_hive_managed table create statement
paragraphs.text:
%spark

spark.sql("SHOW CREATE TABLE hivedb.customer_hive_managed").show(false)

table.tableOptionSpecHash: [{"name":"useFilter","valueType":"boolean","defaultValue":false,"widget":"checkbox","description":"Enable filter for columns"},{"name":"showPagination","valueType":"boolean","defaultValue":false,"widget":"checkbox","description":"Enable pagination for better navigation"},{"name":"showAggregationFooter","valueType":"boolean","defaultValue":false,"widget":"checkbox","description":"Enable a footer for displaying aggregated values"}]

paragraphs.title: Note
paragraphs.text:
%md
The table is stored using the ORC format and it is 'transactional'.

paragraphs.title: Can Spark access that table? No
paragraphs.text:
%md

SELECT * FROM customer_hive_managed

```
org.apache.spark.sql.AnalysisException:
Spark has no access to table `hivedb`.`customer_hive_managed`. Clients can access this table only if
they have the following capabilities: CONNECTORREAD,HIVEFULLACIDREAD,HIVEFULLACIDWRITE,HIVEMANAGESTATS,HIVECACHEINVALIDATE,CONNECTORWRITE.
This table may be a Hive-managed ACID table, or require some other capability that Spark
currently does not implement
...
```

There used to be a solution called the Hive Warehouse Connector with Spark 2, it seems that it has not been carried over to Spark 3.
There are projects in progress to plug that gap but no solution has emerged yet.

paragraphs.title: Can Hive access the tables created using Spark? Yes
paragraphs.text:
%jdbc(hive)

SELECT * FROM sparkdb.customer_spark_managed LIMIT 5;

paragraphs.text:
%md

For the time being, the best practice is to transform and load your data using Spark in a staging area of Hive and then create the corresponding managed tables using HiveQL CTAS statements.

But watch this space as this is a fast evolving area of Spark.
